title: Flowise upsert-history -- T1005 a single unscoped GET returns every tenant's vector-store configuration in one response
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-70473 (GHSA-fr6g-7cq8-fg82),
affecting Flowise's upsert-history endpoint.

`GET /api/v1/upsert-history` returns the entire SERVER-WIDE upsert
history rather than scoping the response to the requesting user's
workspace or tenant. The vendor's own proof of concept against a
production instance produced a response over 100MB, containing
integration parameters and infrastructure details for every
workspace's vector stores -- Qdrant server URLs, collection names,
vector dimensions, content/metadata payload keys -- with no
pagination and no authorization scoping.

Detection logic flags a `GET /api/v1/upsert-history` response whose
body size exceeds a threshold far larger than any single workspace's
history should produce -- the exact `>100MB` disproportionate-response
signal this advisory's proof of concept measured against a live,
multi-tenant production instance.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (FlowiseAI, via
GHSA, citing the affected endpoint, a response excerpt showing
concrete leaked Qdrant configuration, and a reproducible curl-based
proof of concept with an observed response size), fixed in Flowise 3.1.3 (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
